A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Transformer+CoT state-tracking study. All 18 pages of v1 and 19 pages of v3, including their appendices, equations, tables, and figures, support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original architecture comparisons, activation-patching and neuron-probing experiments, and tests of skipping, scratchpad noise, and length generalization.

after.justification: v3 retains original experimental results and reports revised or more detailed findings from the mechanistic and robustness analyses.

M1.justification: The Transformer+CoT procedure, activation patching, neuron classification, and compression/distinction metrics are retained. Although Algorithm 1 disappears, Appendix D retains its substantive steps and the same 0.2 classification threshold. Newly documented training details do not establish a method change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate synthetic word problems over Z60, A4 × Z5, and A5, retaining token tagging, language modeling, group-mixing, skipping, noise, and length-generalization coverage. OpenWebMath supplies a new illustrative example, not a new model-evaluation benchmark. Revised length ranges concern experimental settings.

E2.justification: The comparator sets in Figure 2 and Table 1 remain unchanged. However, v3 removes v1 Appendix C's report that an LSTM used as a decoder failed to converge, and Section 5.3 newly reports a qualitative comparison of NoPE against absolute and relative positional embeddings.

E3.justification: The length-error analysis changes from training on lengths 10–20 and testing at 8 and 25 (v1 Figure 10) to training on 2–20 and testing at 30 (v3 Figure 8). The FSA heatmap captions also change the analyzed layers from MLP10 to MLP11 for GPT2-small and MLP35 for GPT2-large. These are reported setting revisions; reruns are not established.

E4.justification: v3 removes the attention-masking experiment in v1 Appendix I that tested dependence between the two attention patterns. It revises the length-generalization neuron analysis and adds a qualitative positional-encoding comparison. The core skipping and noise interventions remain; the new noise heatmaps largely visualize tests already described in v1.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Newly specified average scores do not introduce uncertainty estimation, and the expected random-F1 derivation is retained.

E6.justification: v3 adds explicit recovery scores of 0.991 and 0.992/0.997, and noise-probing accuracies of 0.943 and 0.379. It replaces the length-neuron results, revises the reported U-turn margin, and removes the attention-masking and decoder-LSTM findings. Figure 2's results, the 0.017-to-0.896 noise-training finding, and Table 1 remain substantively unchanged; Table 1 only changes rounding.

T1.justification: v3 omits v1's explicit log-precision restriction on transformers. It also supplies an explicit monoid-induced FSA construction and a definition of solvable groups. The group-generation theorem and proof, compression/distinction definitions, and random-F1 derivation remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The three central contributions remain: Transformer+CoT's state-tracking capability, evidence for FSA-like representations in late-layer MLP neurons, and robustness to skipping and noise alongside weak length generalization. Rewording and additional supporting detail do not materially redefine these claims.

C2.justification: v3 adds an OpenWebMath example to motivate imperfect reasoning trajectories and explicitly acknowledges that their prevalence is difficult to quantify. It removes v1 Appendix I's explanation and causal argument connecting the two attention patterns. The principal limitations concerning GPT2 models, synthetic tasks, and length generalization remain.

D1.justification: v3 newly provides a project-code link and substantial reproducibility information. Section 3 specifies the data-generation package, single-layer 512-dimensional comparison models, one million sequences, and training limits. New Appendix C documents the mechanistic model configuration, AdamW settings, learning rate, batch size, bfloat16, two A100 GPUs, and approximate runtime. v1 lacks this level of implementation detail.

R1.justification: v3 replaces the brief general interpretability survey with focused comparisons to expressiveness research and Vafa's world-model metrics. It adds Myhill, Nerode, Brown, and Vaswani references while removing several general interpretability references. This refines the relationship to prior work without fundamentally changing the contribution's positioning.

P1.justification: The introduction, experimental descriptions, mechanistic explanations, and several appendices undergo extensive rewriting. Section 2 becomes Background, MLP mathematics moves there from Section 4.2, a focused Related Work section appears near the conclusion, and the main-text attention discussion moves to an appendix. These substantially revise the narrative structure.

P2.justification: Figures are extensively reformatted, with revised colors, axes, legends, and captions. Figure 4 changes from state-wise stacked contributions to layer-wise averages; attention displays expand from two panels to four; noise-probing heatmaps are added. The algorithm box and model/task table are removed while their substantive descriptions remain, and appendix tables and figures are reorganized.

improvement.justification: The experimental specifications in Section 3 and Appendix C, documented code access, and clearer organization make the retained findings easier to assess and reproduce. However, v3 removes a causal attention test and the decoder-LSTM failure report, while much of its added graphical evidence was already described in v1. The balance supports a limited net quality improvement.
